title: What Drawings Does a House Design Set Include? A Homeowner's Reading Guide
desc: Which drawings a detached house design set includes for permit and construction, what each drawing means, how to read dimensions and levels, and what to check.
summary: Explains a house design drawing set: which drawings are mandatory for a construction permit, which are needed for construction, and what homeowners should check before approving.
body: p

Receiving a thick set of drawings from the design firm, many homeowners just look at the perspective and sign. A basic understanding of each drawing helps you check the layout and dimensions before construction and supervise the contractor more effectively.
h2
1. Drawings required for a construction permit application
p
Under Point a, Clause 3, Article 60 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, the permit file for a detached house of a household or individual includes drawings of:
ul
The site plan of the building on the land plot, with a location diagram of the building;
Floor plans, elevations and main sections;
Foundation plan and foundation sections, with a diagram of connections to external technical infrastructure: water supply, drainage and electricity supply;
Together with a written commitment to ensure safety for adjoining buildings; the result of fire prevention and fighting procedures and the design verification report if required by law.
p
For the submission procedure, see Procedure for a detached house construction permit.
h2
2. Additional drawings needed for construction
p
The permit drawing set is not enough for workers to build from. A construction design set for a house usually also includes:
ul
Detailed architecture: furniture layout plans, details of stairs, doors, bathrooms, floor tiling and ceilings.
Structure: foundations, columns, beams, slabs and stairs with dimensions and reinforcement layout; stating the concrete grade and steel type.
Electrical: sockets, switches, lamps, distribution board, wiring; lightning protection and earthing if any.
Water supply and drainage: supply and drain pipes, locations of the water tank and septic tank, pipe slopes.
Material schedules, technical notes and (if hired) a cost estimate.
h2
3. How to read drawings: the basics
ul
Grid lines (A, B, C… and 1, 2, 3…): the grid that locates columns and walls; all dimensions are measured from the grid lines.
Dimensions are usually in millimeters; check that the overall dimensions match the actual width and length of the land plot.
Levels (marked ±0.000, +3.600…): ±0.000 is usually the ground-floor level; the level difference between two floors is the floor height.
Sections: show floor height, stairs, roof and foundation – where narrow stairs and low ceilings are easy to spot.
Elevations: the shape of the facade, materials, colors, balconies and canopies.
h2
4. What the homeowner should check before approving
ol
Whether the number of rooms and the positions of the kitchen, bathrooms and altar meet the family's needs.
Whether the house lies within the land boundary and the building line according to the planning information.
The number of floors, height and total floor area – these affect who may do the design (Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP) and the grade of the building.
The structural drawings carry the designer's name and signature; the foundation is based on a soil survey rather than just an “estimate”.
The electrical and plumbing drawings match the positions of the equipment you plan to buy.
h2
5. Who may prepare the design file?
p

A house of fewer than 3 floors, no basement, a total floor area under 250 m² and a height under 12 m: the homeowner may organize the design themselves. Larger houses must be done by a qualified, experienced organization or individual; houses of 7 floors or more, or with 2 or more basement levels, must also comply with fire prevention and fighting regulations and standards (Article 10). See also Designing a house yourself: when must you hire a design firm?.
h2
6. Keeping the drawings after construction
p

If changes are made during construction, ask the contractor to update the drawings to match what was built. This set of drawings is very useful when repairing, adding floors, rerouting electricity and water, or carrying out the procedure to record the house on the title certificate. See Construction logs and completion records for a house.
p
Need help reading or preparing a house design drawing set? Contact Quan Construction.
note

This article is for reference; each building needs a survey and design by a qualified person. The contents of the permit file are under Decree 217/2026/ND-CP; the construction drawing contents in Section 2 are professional practice and may differ depending on the design firm.
